summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause with limited incidents: the US carried out what it called limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran is still attacking ships around the strait, and the US blockade of Iranian ports continues while indirect talks go on. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: The US carried out 'limited defensive' strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz after surface-to-air missile threats against US assets (AP, via Al Jazeera, Nov 3); the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported a strike on Qeshm Island as one of a series of limited strikes in recent weeks (via Gulf News). Indirect talks continue; Vice President Vance said there has been progress.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent crude futures were at US$93.82 a barrel, down 80 cents, and WTI at US$86.92 at 04:26 GMT on Thursday, Nov 5 (Reuters, via Yahoo Finance), a fourth day of falls; on Wednesday both fell more than 8%, to their lowest since Aug 31, as traders priced in a possible US-Iran settlement after the US midterms (OilPrice.com; The National).

updates.text: Reuters reported that Iran said three more tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday; UKMTO said at least five vessels have reported incidents since Sunday and counted 35 vessels hit in October, the most of any month of the war. Neither side has announced a breakthrough in the talks with Qatari mediators.
sources: Reuters via Investing.com: Tankers hit in Hormuz as Iran keeps up pressure after US vote

updates.text: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) said a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, on Thursday; the crew's status and the damage were not yet known (AP via KRMG; Anadolu Agency; CBS News).

US officials told Axios that military preparations for a possible resumption of major combat are being completed, which is not an order to strike; separately, Qatari mediators are seeking US and Iranian backing for a draft deal that could restart direct talks within days, with Iran reportedly demanding an end to the US naval blockade and sanctions relief before reopening Hormuz (Gulf News live updates).

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents after using what it called unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz: one tanker struck a mine south of the strait, a supertanker caught fire in the eastern part of the waterway, and a tug helping it also caught fire; no independent confirmation was reported (Reuters via ThePrint and Arab News).

Talks between Washington and Tehran have resumed with Qatar and Pakistan among the mediators, with no clear signal on next steps (The National); President Trump told the Financial Times the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran (OilPrice.com).

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, in a statement quoted by state TV, that four 'non-compliant' oil tankers were destroyed after hitting naval mines in a passage south of the Strait of Hormuz that Iran calls prohibited, and that two other vessels were halted; no independent confirmation was reported (AFP via Daily Sabah; OilPrice.com).
Oil prices fell sharply on Wednesday, with Brent below US$100 a barrel for the first time in nearly a month, as traders bet on a US-Iran deal after the midterm results (NBC News; Invezz).
A senior Iranian official said the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days if Washington met Iran's demands, including lifting oil sanctions and releasing frozen assets (OilPrice.com).

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
